seasonal.safety: If any animal bites or scratches you, tell a grown-up right away.

twoDoors.title: Two doors, one path
twoDoors.lead: Every child can take part. Pick the way in that suits you. Both lead to the same judges and the same certificate.

school.title: Through your school
school.line: Your teacher runs the competition in class. We look after the rest.
school.note: We encourage you to participate through your school.

self.title: On your own
self.line: A parent or guardian signs you up with us. You make your entry at home.
self.note: No school needed. Every student can take part this way.

school.1: Your school signs up with Friends of Animals and names a teacher coordinator.
school.2: The coordinator registers your class for a competition.
school.3: You make your entry at school, on the day.
school.4: Your school’s judges choose up to five entries to send on.

self.1: A parent or guardian registers you on our website.
self.2: You get a participant ID and a registration number.
self.3: You make your entry at home and send us a photo of it.

together.1: Our judges score each entry by its code, never by name.
together.2: Results are published, and everyone who took part gets a certificate.

judging.title: How judging works
judging.lead: Entries can travel through five levels. We start with two, and open the others as more schools join.

levelNotes.SCHOOL: Your school’s round. Only on the school route.
levelNotes.NATIONAL: Our final round. Entries from schools and from students on their own meet here.

judging.pathLabel: Judging levels, from school to global
judging.rubricLabel: Share of the score for each part of the judging guide
judging.blind: Judges see the entry code, not your name, school or city.

certificate.title: A certificate for everyone
certificate.lead: Every child who takes part gets a participation certificate with its own number. Schools download them for their students; families download them from their account.
certificate.heading: Certificate of participation
certificate.nameNote: We print a child’s first name and the initial of their surname. Never a photo, an age or an address.

counters.title: So far
counters.asOf: Counted on {date}. Counts under 10 are not shown, and larger counts are rounded down to the nearest 10.

labels.participants: children and young people took part
